description: Canada study visa from Pakistan: requirements, documents, fees, timeline, common mistakes and FAQ. Honest guidance by SK Immigration Services, Rawalpindi.

faqs.question: What are Canada study permit requirements from Pakistan?
faqs.answer: DLI acceptance (and PAL when required), funds, identity docs, biometrics/medicals as asked, and a coherent study plan. SK Immigration prepares the file; IRCC decides.

faqs.question: Do I need a GIC?
faqs.answer: Many applicants use a GIC as part of funds evidence, especially for certain pathways — confirm what your intake and school expect. We map funds options during consultation.

faqs.question: Is IELTS required for Canada study?
faqs.answer: Schools and IRCC pathways often expect language scores. Exact tests and bands depend on the DLI and programme — we confirm before you book expensive tests.

faqs.question: How long does Canada study permit take?
faqs.answer: Often 3–8+ months. Incomplete SOPs and funds are the usual delays we fix before submission.

faqs.question: SK Immigration Canada study fee?
faqs.answer: From PKR 50,000 for preparation. IRCC and school fees are separate. No guarantees.

faqs.question: Do you guarantee the study permit?
faqs.answer: No. IRCC decides. We prepare honest, complete applications.

Canada study permit from Pakistan — what actually matters

IRCC looks at programme fit, funds, and a coherent study plan — not agent slogans. You need a letter of acceptance from a Designated Learning Institution (DLI). Some intakes also need a Provincial Attestation Letter (PAL). SK Immigration builds the narrative and checklist; IRCC decides every study permit.

Requirements

  • Letter of acceptance from a DLI (and PAL when your programme/intake requires it)
  • Proof of funds covering tuition + living (GIC and/or bank evidence as applicable)
  • Study plan / SOP that matches your academics and career logic
  • Biometrics for Pakistani applicants; medicals when required
  • Passport and complete IRCC online forms

Process we follow

  1. Eligibility and budget review — Canada vs Europe if funds or marks are tight
  2. DLI shortlist and admission support
  3. Funds / GIC planning and SOP coaching
  4. IRCC packaging, biometrics appointment help
  5. Additional document responses and decision follow-up

Documents

  • Letter of acceptance (+ PAL if required)
  • Passport and photos
  • Proof of funds / GIC confirmation
  • SOP, CV and academic transcripts
  • Police certificates / medicals when requested

Interactive checklist: Open Canada checklist →

Fees

IRCC study permit fee + biometrics + medicals + GIC/tuition proofs. SK packages from PKR 50,000 for preparation support only.

Timeline

Often 3–8+ months depending on IRCC queues, medicals and how complete the first submission is. Peak September intakes need earlier starts.

Common mistakes for Pakistan files

  • Study plan that reads as immigration-first instead of education-first
  • Funds that look borrowed or unexplained
  • Programme choice that does not fit prior academics
  • Missing biometrics or medical deadlines
  • Confusing visitor entry with study permit pathways

Canada study permit from Pakistan — DLI, funds, intent

Canada study files succeed when the school is a designated learning institution (DLI), the programme makes sense for your history, and funds/intent are consistent. IRCC decides every study permit; SK Immigration prepares documents and honest risk review.

What you typically need

  • Letter of acceptance from a DLI
  • Proof of funds for tuition + living (and GIC where your pathway uses one — verify current programme rules)
  • Language results if the school/IRCC pathway requires them
  • SOP / study plan that explains Canada specifically
  • Biometrics and medicals when requested

Process outline

  1. DLI shortlist and applications
  2. Acceptance + deposit planning
  3. Funds packaging (history matters more than a one-day balance)
  4. Study permit application + biometrics
  5. Decision and travel / PAL or province-specific steps when applicable — verify current IRCC pages

Common refusal themes we coach against

  • Programme mismatch with prior academics or career story
  • Funds that appear borrowed or unexplained
  • Weak home ties / unclear post-study intent narrative
  • Agents promising “guaranteed Canada visa”
